findings.title: Unsubscribe crashes when no TopicUser row exists
findings.body: TopicsController#unsubscribe calls TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id]) and immediately reads tu.notification_level. If the current user has no topic_users row for that topic (for example they never visited the topic, the row was removed, or the URL is visited directly), find_by returns nil and the action raises NoMethodError instead of handling the unsubscribe. Use find_or_initialize_by, or TopicUser.change, so a missing row is created or handled safely.

findings.title: State-changing unsubscribe is performed by an unauthenticated GET
findings.body: The new /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe endpoint changes the user's topic notification level in response to a GET request, skips the XHR check, and has no token or confirmation. Because Rails CSRF protection does not apply to GET requests, a third-party page can cause a logged-in user to mute or downgrade notifications for arbitrary topic IDs by loading an image or link. Email prefetching or link previews can also trigger the change unintentionally. Use a POST/PUT action, a signed per-user unsubscribe token, or at least require an explicit confirmation step.

findings.title: Direct TopicUser save bypasses notification-change side effects
findings.body: TopicsController#unsubscribe updates the TopicUser record directly and calls save!, bypassing TopicUser.change. TopicUser.change is the normal path for notification-level changes and sets notifications_changed_at/notifications_reason_id and publishes the notification_level_change MessageBus event. With the direct save, open clients will not be notified of the new notification level, and the reason/audit metadata for the change is lost. It also does not handle the missing-row case the way TopicUser.change does.

findings.title: track_visit! uses the topic id as the user id when passed an id
findings.body: TopicUser.track_visit! computes user_id as `user.is_a?(User) ? user.id : topic`. When the second argument is a user id integer, as in TopicsController#track_visit_to_topic (`TopicUser.track_visit! topic_id, user_id`), the method assigns the topic id to user_id. This creates or updates topic_users rows for the wrong user, corrupting visit tracking and potentially notification-related state. The else branch should return `user`, not `topic`.

findings.title: Shared unsubscribe_link now requires unsubscribe_url for all callers
findings.body: The shared `unsubscribe_link` translation now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`. Email::MessageBuilder renders this translation for any email built with `add_unsubscribe_link`, but only `UserNotifications#send_notification_email` was updated to supply `unsubscribe_url`. Any other current/future caller or plugin that enables the unsubscribe link without providing `unsubscribe_url` will fail email rendering/sending with a missing interpolation argument. Make the per-topic line conditional, provide a default, or update all callers.

findings.title: No specs for the new unsubscribe endpoint
findings.body: The PR adds a state-changing TopicsController#unsubscribe endpoint but includes no controller/request specs. Important cases are untested: missing TopicUser row, slug mismatch redirects, JSON vs HTML behavior, permission handling, and the fact that the action mutates notification state. A spec would catch the nil TopicUser crash and the missing MessageBus/metadata behavior.
